title: Radius From Circle Area Calculator
description: Find a circle's radius and diameter from its area with the Radius From Circle Area Calculator — r = √(A ÷ π), in any area unit. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a circular service area of 100 km² has a radius of 5.64 km — and a one-acre circle, all 43,560 square feet of it, has a radius of just 117.8 feet.
quick_answer: The Radius From Circle Area Calculator inverts the area formula: radius equals the square root of area divided by pi. Enter the circle's area and read the radius — plus diameter and circumference — for coverage areas, tanks and plots.

body.t: A provider claims '314 square miles of coverage' from one site — that is a 10-mile radius wearing an area costume. The forward family starts at the
Floor area known from a spec sheet, diameter needed for a lid, liner or foundation: the radius is the hinge number between them.
Circular sample plots are forestry's standard: a 1/10-acre plot's radius (37.2 ft) is a number cruisers carry in their heads — this page is where it comes from.
Pizza value comparisons are area comparisons (a 16-inch pizza is two 8-inch pizzas doubled, not quadrupled — area again). The radius keeps the menu honest.
An area of exactly π km² (3.14159) gives a radius of exactly 1 km — the formula's party trick, and a clean check that the calculator's inverse is honest.

1 acre = 43,560 sq ft; r = √(43,560 ÷ π) = 117.8 ft, diameter 235.5 ft. A circular acre fits inside a square acre (208.7 ft sides) with room to spare — circles pack less than squares, as every pizza already knows.

popular_table.intro: Computed r = √(A/π) across the units circles arrive in.
popular_table.note: Radius grows with the square root of area: quadruple the area, double the radius. Every 'huge' area claim deflates through this root — the calculator is the deflator.

faq: r = √(A ÷ π), the algebraic inverse of A = πr². Diameter is 2r; circumference is 2πr — the page returns the family, since callers rarely want the radius alone.
Square feet, square metres, acres, hectares, square kilometres and square miles — converted internally so the radius arrives in the matching length unit.
Can I go the other way (radius to area)?
Yes — the Circle Area From Radius Calculator is the forward lane, and the pair of pages round-trip exactly.
My area is a radius in disguise from a map tool.
Common: a 'coverage area' exported from a radius map. Recovering the radius lets you redraw the same circle in the Map Radius tool and compare like with like.
An ellipse needs two axes; from area alone its radius is undefined. If the shape is a squashed circle, measure both axes on the map and use the ellipse's own geometry.
The root is exact for the input; report the radius at the input's dignity. An area paced off in the field earns a whole-foot radius, not hundredths.
Zero gives a zero radius (a point); negative area is not a thing in this universe, and the calculator declines it accordingly.
